newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end lower on economic news.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end lower on economic news.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed softer as figures showing the economy grew faster than expected in August dashed hopes that interest rates could fall by the end of the year, dealers said.

The bolsa is expected to resume its negative trend at the opening as investors realize there is little chance of the central bank easing its restrictive monetary policy until next year, said Henry Rudnick, head of research at CB Capitales.
"The market does not look very good for the next few days," said Rudnick.
The IPSA index ended down 0.45 percent at 99.7 points.
The general IGPA index shed 0.33 percent to 5,439.12 points.
Turnover rose to 12 billion pesos from 9.2 billion pesos on Tuesday.
News that the economy expanded 5.7 percent in August surprised investors who had been expecting growth to be around 4.5-5 percent, said dealers.
Long-term interest rates rose slightly in reaction to the growth figure, said traders.
Losers included telecommunications company Telex on figures showing that its share of the international long-distance market fell to 12.67 percent in August from 14.53 percent in July, they said.
"The company's third quarter earnings are expected to be bad as a result of its falling market share," said one dealer.
Power investment company Enersis fell on fears the company's earnings will be hurt by government plans to cut electricity prices in a review which will take effect next month, said dealers.
